facts.text: The operator is the person who drives and controls a machine, and the cab is the enclosed compartment where the operator sits.
facts.quote: The operator is the person who drives and controls a machine, and the cab is the enclosed compartment where that person sits.

facts.text: A heavy-machine operator steers, works the bucket or blade, watches mirrors and camera screens, listens to the radio, and decides when to move and when to wait.
facts.quote: On a heavy machine the operator steers, works the bucket or blade, watches mirrors and camera screens, listens to the radio and decides when to move and when to wait.

facts.text: A heavy-machine cab is a glass and steel enclosure high above the ground, often on one side of the machine; its pillars can hide a pickup from the operator's view.
facts.quote: The cab is a glass and steel box high above the ground, often on one side, with pillars that can hide a pickup [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Vibration, dust, radio traffic and production pressure are normal conditions for heavy-machine operators.
facts.quote: Vibration, dust, radio traffic and production pressure are normal.

facts.text: The standards keep responsibility with the operator because ISO 21815-1 states that the technology cannot cover every situation.
facts.quote: The standards keep responsibility with the operator, because ISO 21815-1 states that the technology cannot cover every situation [Chapter 4].

facts.text: The operator is identified as the least understood part of the heavy-machine system.
facts.quote: the operator is the least understood part of the system

facts.text: No field-measured distribution of heavy-machine operators' reaction times to proximity warnings was found.
facts.quote: no field-measured distribution of how fast heavy-machine operators react to proximity warnings was found [Chapter 4].

facts.text: The US Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) estimates that adequate seat belts could save three to four miners' lives per year.
facts.quote: MSHA (the US Mine Safety and Health Administration) estimates that three to four miners' lives a year could be saved by adequate seat belts

entities.name: US Mine Safety and Health Administration

facts.text: Seven of 12 drivers killed at dump points were unbelted.
facts.quote: seven of 12 drivers killed at dump points were unbelted [Chapter 4].

facts.text: An automatic brake acts when the operator has not acted, so validating automatic braking requires assumptions about what the operator does and when.
facts.quote: An automatic brake acts when the operator has not, so validating it means assuming something about what the operator does and when.

facts.text: The booklet recommends treating operator response as an uncertain quantity and testing the sensitivity of validation results to operator response.
facts.quote: The booklet advises treating operator response as an uncertain quantity and testing how sensitive results are to it [Chapter 4].
